boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Kenyon study settings, from library reading rooms and an atrium nook to residence-hall lounges and an outdoor patio.

cards.title: Settle In Beneath Two-Story Windows
cards.subtitle: Level 1, Chalmers Library
cards.notes: Bring an extended reading assignment and choose between desks and softer seating; this is Chalmers’ designated 24/7 room.
cards.short_summary: A large, light-filled reading room with desks, armchairs and around-the-clock designation.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon identifies the Level 1 Carver Reading Room as a designated 24/7 space; a College feature documents two-story windows, desks and seating for up to 100.
cards.access_notes: Designated 24/7 space. Open study spaces are first come, first served; consult the library schedule for other services.

cards.title: Work Under the Glass-Art Skylight
cards.subtitle: Central atrium, Chalmers Library
cards.notes: Use this central study-and-gathering space when you want an open setting near library collections and student-support offices.
cards.short_summary: An expansive central study space animated by colored light from its architectural-glass skylight.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon describes Winkler Atrium as both a gathering and study space at the heart of Chalmers Library, beneath an architectural-glass skylight.
cards.access_notes: Open Chalmers study spaces are first come, first served. Check the current library schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Choose the Third-Floor Quiet Room
cards.subtitle: Level 3, Chalmers Library
cards.notes: Head here for quiet individual work in a spacious reading-room setting, then keep conversation and group tasks elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, spacious third-floor reading room documented specifically as a place to study.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon identifies Denniston Reading Room as a quiet, spacious reading room on Chalmers Library’s third floor and calls it a scenic place to study.
cards.access_notes: The library designates quiet reading rooms on Level 3. Check current building hours before arrival.

cards.title: Take the Highest Atrium Overlook
cards.subtitle: Upper crow’s nest, Chalmers Library
cards.notes: Pick this named upper-level crow’s nest for focused work with an overlook; use library maps to locate it before settling in.
cards.short_summary: The topmost of Chalmers’ distinctive crow’s-nest study spaces overlooking the atrium.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon documents crow’s-nest study spaces overlooking the Chalmers atrium and identifies the top space as the Toft Loft.
cards.access_notes: Open library study spaces are first come, first served. Consult Chalmers maps and current building hours.

cards.title: Study Beside the Collections
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Chalmers Library
cards.notes: Bring research that benefits from nearby stacks and use this named lower-level room for a quieter, collection-adjacent session.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level reading room near Chalmers’ book collections and Special Collections and Archives.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon’s library dedication feature names the Lower Level Reading Room and places it on a lower level containing the collections, quiet study spots and Special Collections and Archives.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to Chalmers building hours. Special Collections and Archives maintains separate service access.

cards.title: Spread Out at a Long Wooden Table
cards.subtitle: Top floor, Ascension Hall
cards.notes: Climb to Ascension’s top floor when a long table suits drafting or problem sets; armchairs offer an alternative for reading.
cards.short_summary: A spacious top-floor study lounge combining long wooden tables with cozy armchairs.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon identifies Nu Pi Kappa as a spacious top-floor study lounge in Ascension Hall, furnished with cozy armchairs and long wooden tables.
cards.access_notes: The public page does not specify hours or entry rules; confirm current Ascension Hall access before visiting.

cards.title: Claim a High-Backed Study Chair
cards.subtitle: Second floor, McBride Hall
cards.notes: Use the long table for shared work or choose a high-backed chair when you need more visual separation in the communal room.
cards.short_summary: A renovated residence-hall lounge purposefully divided into study and social settings.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon reports that McBride Hall’s second-floor communal room was re-envisioned as a study space with a long table, comfortable seating and high-backed chairs.
cards.access_notes: Located inside a residence hall; the source does not publish entry rules, so residents and visitors should follow current housing access policy.

cards.title: Pair Group Work With Private Seating
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Mather Hall
cards.notes: Meet at the long study table for collaboration, or switch to a high-backed seat when the assignment turns to solo work.
cards.short_summary: A renovated communal room offering both a shared study table and more private seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon reports that Mather Hall’s second-floor communal room became a study space with a long table, comfortable seating and high-backed chairs for added privacy.
cards.access_notes: Located inside a residence hall; the source does not publish entry rules, so residents and visitors should follow current housing access policy.

cards.title: Set Up in a Softer Lounge Setting
cards.subtitle: Gund Residence Hall
cards.notes: Choose among varied seating for reading or laptop work; keep the meditation cushions available for their intended quiet use.
cards.short_summary: A large residence-hall lounge refreshed with varied furniture, rugs, lamps, plants and meditation cushions.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon documents the named Gunderdome lounge in Gund Residence Hall as a large space furnished with varied seating, rugs, lamps, plants and meditation cushions.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Gund Residence Hall; the source does not state public access or hours. Follow current residential entry policy.

cards.title: Take the Assignment Outdoors
cards.subtitle: Outside Gund Commons
cards.notes: Bring work suited to an outdoor session and use the tables, chairs or Adirondack rockers; have an indoor fallback for weather.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus patio furnished with tables, chairs and Adirondack rockers.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon reports that the patio outside Gund Commons received new outdoor furniture, including tables, chairs and Adirondack rockers.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor seating is weather-dependent. The source does not publish hours or reservation requirements.
